choices.why: This is the only truly beige option, a clean-lined track-arm sofa with a low profile and dark wood legs that fits the serene Japandi look against the right wall.
At 160x230 cm this natural jute rug is big enough to anchor both the sofa and the coffee table, and its warm texture softens the dark floor.
This low, simple round table in warm wood is the most Japandi option, without the gold metal of the alternative or the black finish of the other.
This is the only paper lantern floor lamp, and it gives the soft, sculptural light the user asked for in the corner beside the sofa.
The braided money tree is the largest, most architectural plant and suits the corner by the balcony glass; ideally it should be moved from its nursery pot into a neutral ceramic pot.

answer.why: Beige, jute, warm wood and paper share a neutral, natural palette that stands out softly against the white walls and dark floor. Each piece is simple and low, keeping the room calm and uncluttered as the user asked.
